- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

442	+## The invariant: every supported CSR is tested or named-excluded
443	+
444	+Registration passes only if every `implemented` CSR falls in exactly one bucket,
445	+each machine-checked:
446	+- **transported + tested** -- restored at resume, drained, `--verify`-compared,
447	+  AND has its own per-CSR test (write-survival, read-back, or a named covered/
448	+  verify-only disposition).
449	+- **named-excluded** -- not transported, with a named reason
450	+  (`CONST_RO`, `EXCL_*`, or a `gate=off` for a feature this config lacks).
451	+
452	+Neither-bucket = silent state loss = FAIL. Transported without a test = FAIL.
453	+See `docs/engine_registration_completeness_ROADMAP.md`.
454	+
455	 ## What must pass (checks, before "supported")
456	 
457	 1. vsim caps unit test modeling this engine's config shape

@@ -356,11 +356,25 @@ Example invocation (marker mode, just the minimal arg):
 | `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
 | `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
 | `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
+| `--drain-minimal`             | Exit drain reads back only mcycle/minstret; the driver sets it when `--verify` is off. |
+| `--no-reset-baseline`         | Disable the liveness gate (below): restore every transported register. |
 | `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (ICEman or OpenOCD). The hart free-runs; the debugger halts it over the JTAG DTM on connect. The `./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb` path opens this port for ICEman (set `$ICEMAN`). |
 | `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |
 
 The default for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the `virt` / `andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.
 
+**Liveness gate (reset baseline).** Every register moved through the Debug
+Module costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most transported state still
+holds its reset value. So the resume skips any restore whose drained value
+equals the engine's own reset value -- a no-op write. The very first hybrid
+run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair drains that reset state once (a few
+extra seconds) and caches it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/` (fallback
+`~/.cache/andesim/`); later runs load the cache and typically cut the vsim
+leg by ~4x (hello: 50k -> 12k simulated cycles). The cache self-invalidates
+on engine rebuild or ELF change (mtime+size keyed); delete the directory to
+force a fresh capture. `--verify` works unchanged with the gate active;
+`--no-reset-baseline` restores the old transport-everything behavior.
+
 Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
 license-gated and off by default).
 
@@ -817,11 +831,15 @@ hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
 
 Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
 (the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
-over the Debug Module -- ~190 abstract commands (all FPRs, the vector-register
-sweep, the Andes/M-ext CSR blocks) whose simulated debug cycles dominate hybrid
-wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count. `--verify` needs
-every field for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to
-take noticeably longer than the same run without it.
+over the Debug Module. On a full drain the GPR and FPR readback ride
+Program-Buffer sweeps into the shared scratch page (like the vector-register
+sweep) -- ~6 halted-hart round-trips each instead of 31/32 per-register abstract
+commands -- and the Andes/M-ext CSR blocks ride a batched `csrr`+`sd` sweep the
+same way (3 CSRs per Program-Buffer execution), so what remains is the scalar
+M-mode CSRs, whose simulated debug cycles dominate hybrid wall-clock for a short
+ROI but never affect the cycle count. `--verify` needs every field for the diff,
+so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to take noticeably longer
+than the same run without it.
 
 How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
 oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
@@ -869,6 +887,16 @@ complete per-CSR disposition for all 232 spec CSRs is in
 `docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, guarded against drift by
 `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`.
 
+Per-engine CSR validation is a registration requirement: every supported
+engine build carries its own CSR manifest + registration report under
+`tests/engines/` (contract: `tests/engines/README.md`).
+`docs/engine_registration_tutorial.ipynb` walks the whole lifecycle --
+the three-way audit (spec x config.inc x RTL), registering a new engine or
+config, and removing one. `docs/csr_transport_bringup_tutorial.ipynb` is the
+companion reference: what the `/csr-transport-bringup` skill does (its 7-phase
+pipeline), every column of `csr_manifest.csv`, and each file a registration
+ships under `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash>/`.

 Costs and limits: the oracle leg is one extra QEMU run of the whole
 program (MHz-class -- cheap next to the vsim leg). `--verify` works with
 `--trigger marker|pc`, assumes the single-shot ROI the hybrid run itself

+## The invariant: every supported CSR is tested or named-excluded
+
+Registration passes only if every `implemented` CSR falls in exactly one bucket,
+each machine-checked:
+- **transported + tested** -- restored at resume, drained, `--verify`-compared,
+  AND has its own per-CSR test (write-survival, read-back, or a named covered/
+  verify-only disposition).
+- **named-excluded** -- not transported, with a named reason
+  (`CONST_RO`, `EXCL_*`, or a `gate=off` for a feature this config lacks).
+
+Neither-bucket = silent state loss = FAIL. Transported without a test = FAIL.
+See `docs/engine_registration_completeness_ROADMAP.md`.
+
 ## What must pass (checks, before "supported")
 
 1. vsim caps unit test modeling this engine's config shape

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Registration completeness gate (ROADMAP F1): the under-claim HARD check.

Rule: in a registered engine's csr_manifest.csv, every IMPLEMENTED CSR must be
either TRANSPORTED, or carry a named reason for not being transported --
`CONST_RO` (a read-only constant, nothing to restore) or an `EXCL_*` class
(mode/rv32/debug/sidefx/... a documented exclusion). An implemented,
non-transported CSR with neither is an UNDER-CLAIM: its value is silently lost
across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. That FAILS registration.

Only `transported == no` is the hard fail. `transported == partial` (e.g. even
pmpcfg, pmaaddr0-15) is an intentional, disposition-documented subset, not an
under-claim. The `implemented` column is the engine's real existent set (today
from gen_manifest.py's RTL eval; ROADMAP F3 makes it the live probe) -- this
gate is only as trustworthy as that column, and self-truthing once F3 lands.

Usage:
  check_completeness.py [manifest.csv ...]   # check the given manifests
  check_completeness.py                       # default: every registered manifest

Exit 0 = clean; 1 = at least one under-claim (each printed with its evidence).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def accepted_reason(disposition: str) -> bool:
    """A named reason an IMPLEMENTED CSR may legitimately go untransported."""
    d = disposition.strip()
    return d.startswith("CONST_RO") or d.startswith("EXCL_")


def scan(path: str) -> tuple[int, list[dict]]:
    impl = 0
    under: list[dict] = []
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            if r["implemented"] not in ("yes", "partial"):
                continue
            impl += 1
            if r["transported"] == "no" and not accepted_reason(r["gate_or_disposition"]):
                under.append(r)
    return impl, under


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    paths = argv[1:] or sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(HERE, "*", "csr_manifest.csv")))
    if not paths:
        print("[completeness] no manifests found")
        return 0

    total_impl = 0
    fails = 0
    for p in paths:
        impl, under = scan(p)
        total_impl += impl
        rel = os.path.relpath(p, HERE)
        for r in under:
            print(
                f"UNDER-CLAIM {r['addr']} {r['name']}: implemented={r['implemented']} "
                f"transported=no disposition={r['gate_or_disposition']!r} -- implemented "
                f"but not transported and no CONST_RO/EXCL_* reason  ({rel})"
            )
            fails += 1

    if fails:
        print(f"[completeness] FAIL: {fails} under-claim(s) across {len(paths)} manifest(s)")
        return 1
    print(
        f"[completeness] all clean: {len(paths)} manifest(s), "
        f"{total_impl} implemented CSR-rows, 0 under-claims"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Registration test-coverage gate (ROADMAP F2): every TRANSPORTED CSR must have
a per-CSR test disposition in safe_write_policy.csv.

Allowed dispositions (actions):
  write       -- generated write-survival fixture (csr_survival_gen.S): write a
                 distinctive value pre-ROI, prove restore in-ROI, rewrite for the
                 drain, --verify compares.
  readback    -- generated read-back round-trip fixture (csr_survival_gen.S): read
                 the value pre-ROI, prove it survived resume in-ROI. No write --
                 for control CSRs that are unsafe to blind-write but safe to read.
  covered     -- an existing engine-generic fixture already round-trips it.
  verify-only -- no dedicated fixture is possible (counter / HW-driven / reset-
                 divergent / passthrough); --verify on real workloads is the
                 coverage, with the reason recorded in the policy.

A transported CSR whose policy action is missing or anything else (e.g. the
retired `skip`) is UNTESTED -> FAIL. F1 (check_completeness.py) enforces the
implemented->transported direction; this enforces transported->tested. Together
they are "every supported CSR completely tested."

Usage:
  check_test_coverage.py [manifest.csv ...]   # default: every registered manifest
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import glob
import os
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ALLOWED = {"write", "readback", "covered", "verify-only"}


def polname(name: str) -> str:
    """Manifest CSR name -> safe_write_policy key (range rows collapse to the low
    member, matching gen_fixtures.py)."""
    m = re.match(r"^(.*?)(\d+)~(\d+)$", name)
    return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}" if m else name


def load_policy() -> dict[str, str]:
    p = os.path.join(HERE, "safe_write_policy.csv")
    return {r["name"]: r["action"] for r in csv.DictReader(open(p))}


def scan(path: str, policy: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int, list[tuple[str, str, object]]]:
    n = 0
    miss: list[tuple[str, str, object]] = []
    for r in csv.DictReader(open(path, newline="")):
        if r["transported"] not in ("yes", "partial") or not r["access"].endswith("RW"):
            continue
        n += 1
        act = policy.get(polname(r["name"]))
        if act not in ALLOWED:
            miss.append((r["addr"], r["name"], act))
    return n, miss


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    policy = load_policy()
    paths = argv[1:] or sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(HERE, "*", "csr_manifest.csv")))
    if not paths:
        print("[coverage] no manifests found")
        return 0

    fails = 0
    total = 0
    for p in paths:
        n, miss = scan(p, policy)
        total += n
        rel = os.path.relpath(p, HERE)
        for addr, name, act in miss:
            print(
                f"UNTESTED {addr} {name}: transported but policy action={act!r} "
                f"not in {sorted(ALLOWED)}  ({rel})"
            )
            fails += 1

    if fails:
        print(f"[coverage] FAIL: {fails} transported CSR(s) without a test disposition")
        return 1
    print(
        f"[coverage] all covered: {len(paths)} manifest(s), {total} transported RW "
        f"CSR-rows, each write/readback/covered/verify-only"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F3: probe an engine's CSR existence + reset values on the live RTL.
3	#
4	# Halts the freshly-reset hart via the Debug Module and checked-reads every
5	# inventory CSR (cmderr => not implemented). Emits "0xADDR,yes|no,0xRESET" CSV
6	# to stdout. Feed it to gen_manifest.py via ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV to MEASURE the
7	# implemented set + reset values instead of hand-tracing RTL params `P`:
8	#
9	#   tests/engines/probe_engine.sh ax45mpv_premium > /tmp/probe.csv
10	#   ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV=/tmp/probe.csv \
11	#     python3 tests/engines/<engine>-<hash>/gen_manifest.py <regdir>
12	#
13	# Read-side-effect CSRs (EXCL_SIDEFX) are excluded from the probe list -- reading
14	# them perturbs state -- so gen_manifest falls back to the RTL equation for
15	# those few. Usage: probe_engine.sh <engine>
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
19	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
21	[ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] && . "$ROOT/config.env"
22	VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"
23	TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf"
24	
25	engine="${1:?usage: probe_engine.sh <engine>}"
26	SIM="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_$engine"
27	[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "no sim binary at $SIM (build vsim first)"
28	
29	WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
30	# 1) spin ELF: a benign, mapped reset vector -- the hart free-runs a couple
31	#    instructions before the DMI halt takes effect; an unmapped vector bus-errors.
32	printf '.section .text\n.globl _start\n_start:\n1:\tj 1b\n' > "$WORK/spin.S"
33	"${TC}-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -c "$WORK/spin.S" -o "$WORK/spin.o" \
34	  || fail "spin.S assemble failed"
35	"${TC}-ld" -T "$ROOT/runtime/andesim.ld" -nostdlib -static "$WORK/spin.o" -o "$WORK/spin.elf" \
36	  || fail "spin.elf link failed"

38	python3 - "$ROOT" > "$WORK/addrs.txt" <<'PY'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3: probe an engine's CSR existence + reset values on the live RTL.
#
# Halts the freshly-reset hart via the Debug Module and checked-reads every
# inventory CSR (cmderr => not implemented). Emits "0xADDR,yes|no,0xRESET" CSV
# to stdout. Feed it to gen_manifest.py via ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV to MEASURE the
# implemented set + reset values instead of hand-tracing RTL params `P`:
#
#   tests/engines/probe_engine.sh ax45mpv_premium > /tmp/probe.csv
#   ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV=/tmp/probe.csv \
#     python3 tests/engines/<engine>-<hash>/gen_manifest.py <regdir>
#
# Read-side-effect CSRs (EXCL_SIDEFX) are excluded from the probe list -- reading
# them perturbs state -- so gen_manifest falls back to the RTL equation for
# those few. Usage: probe_engine.sh <engine>
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
[ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] && . "$ROOT/config.env"
VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"
TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf"

engine="${1:?usage: probe_engine.sh <engine>}"
SIM="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_$engine"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "no sim binary at $SIM (build vsim first)"

WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# 1) spin ELF: a benign, mapped reset vector -- the hart free-runs a couple
#    instructions before the DMI halt takes effect; an unmapped vector bus-errors.
printf '.section .text\n.globl _start\n_start:\n1:\tj 1b\n' > "$WORK/spin.S"
"${TC}-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -c "$WORK/spin.S" -o "$WORK/spin.o" \
  || fail "spin.S assemble failed"
"${TC}-ld" -T "$ROOT/runtime/andesim.ld" -nostdlib -static "$WORK/spin.o" -o "$WORK/spin.elf" \
  || fail "spin.elf link failed"
# 2) probe address list = full inventory MINUS read-side-effect CSRs.
python3 - "$ROOT" > "$WORK/addrs.txt" <<'PY'
import csv, re, sys
root = sys.argv[1]
def expand(s):
    s = s.strip(); m = re.match(r'^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)~(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$', s)
    if not m: return [int(s, 16)] if re.match(r'^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+$', s) else []
    lo = int(m.group(1), 16); h = m.group(2)
    hi = int(m.group(1)[:len(m.group(1))-len(h)] + h, 16) if len(h) < len(m.group(1)) else int(h, 16)
    return list(range(lo, hi + 1))
sidefx = set()
for r in csv.DictReader(open(root + '/tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv')):
    if r.get('decision') == 'EXCL_SIDEFX': sidefx |= set(expand(r['addr']))
addrs = set()
for r in csv.DictReader(open(root + '/tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv')):
    addrs |= {a for a in expand(r['addr']) if a not in sidefx}
print('\n'.join('0x%03X' % a for a in sorted(addrs)))
PY
# 3) probe: halt the reset hart, checked-read each address.
"$SIM" --probe "$WORK/addrs.txt" "$WORK/spin.elf" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^0x'

12	    (crosschecked against scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py -- parity OK)
13	  - reset values: the reset-baseline capture ~/.cache/andesim/*.bin
14	    (hybrid_state_v1, drained from the freshly reset halted hart; fields the
15	    drain does not read stay zero and are reported as "-")
16	  - over-claim proof: the cold-cache hybrid --verify run (PB csr sweep of the
17	    full claimed set faulted on nothing; [state-diff] PASS 145 fields)
18	"""
19	import csv, re, struct, sys, glob, os
20	
21	AND = "/home/nick/work/andesim"
22	VS  = "/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim"
23	DEC = VS + "/build/Vax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v"

27	# (addr,yes|no,0xreset), MEASURE implemented + reset from it instead of the
28	# hand-traced RTL params P (below) and the ELF-keyed baseline capture. The two
29	# agree on this engine (validated: 0 existence mismatches, all reset values
30	# identical); the probe removes the manual P transcription.
31	_probe = {}
32	if os.getenv("ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV"):
33	    for _ln in open(os.getenv("ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV")):
34	        _c = _ln.strip().split(",")
35	        if len(_c) == 3 and _c[0].startswith("0x"):
36	            _probe[int(_c[0], 16)] = (_c[1] == "yes",

41	# config.inc values shown in the trace (ICACHE 64K, DCACHE 64K, all ECC none,

57	    expr = re.sub(r"12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)", lambda m: "0x" + m.group(1), expr)
58	    return expr.replace("1'b0", "0").replace("1'b1", "1")

62	      re.findall(r"localparam\s+(CSR12_\w+)\s*=\s*12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*;", src)}

94	    "mxstatus":0x7C4,"mpft_ctl":0x7C5,"mclk_ctl":0x7DF,"milmb":0x7C0,

99	    "mhpmcounter3":0xB03,"mhpmcounter4":0xB04,"mhpmcounter5":0xB05,
100	    "mhpmcounter6":0xB06,"mhpmevent3":0x323,"mhpmevent4":0x324,
101	    "mhpmevent5":0x325,"mhpmevent6":0x326,"mcounterwen":0x7CE,
102	    "mcounterinten":0x7CF,"mcountermask_s":0x7D2,"mcountermask_u":0x7D3,
103	    "mnscratch":0x740,"mnepc":0x741,"mncause":0x742,"mnstatus":0x744,
104	    "mnvec":0x7C3,"mrnxvec":0x7DE,"mdcause":0x7C9,"mslideleg":0x7D5,
105	    "msavestatus":0x7D6,"msaveepc1":0x7D7,"msavecause1":0x7D8,
106	    "msaveepc2":0x7D9,"msavecause2":0x7DA,"msavedcause1":0x7DB,
107	    "msavedcause2":0x7DC,"mtvt":0x307,"mintthresh":0x347,"mcirq_entry":0x7EC,
108	    "mstateen0":0x30C,"mstateen1":0x30D,"mstateen2":0x30E,"mstateen3":0x30F,
109	    "mcctlbeginaddr":0x7CB,"mcctldata":0x7CD,"mppib":0x7F0,"mfiob":0x7F1,
110	    "tselect":0x7A0,"tdata1":0x7A1,"tdata2":0x7A2,"tcontrol":0x7A5,
111	    "mcontext":0x7A8,"uzobctl":0x808,"ucctlbeginaddr":0x80B,
112	    "sleepvalue":0x811,"umisc_ctl":0x813,
113	}
114	claimed = set()
115	for n in DESCRIBE:
116	    if n == "pmacfg":   claimed |= {0xBC0, 0xBC2}
117	    elif n == "pmaaddr": claimed |= set(range(0xBD0, 0xBE0))

317	def expand(addr_field):
318	    """inventory addr string -> list of ints"""
319	    s = addr_field.strip()
320	    m = re.match(r"^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$", s)
321	    if m: return [int(m.group(1), 16)]
322	    m = re.match(r"^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)~(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$", s)
323	    if m:
324	        lo = int(m.group(1), 16); hi_s = m.group(2)
325	        hi = int(m.group(1)[: len(m.group(1)) - len(hi_s)] + hi_s, 16) \
326	             if len(hi_s) < len(m.group(1)) else int(hi_s, 16)
327	        return list(range(lo, hi + 1))
328	    raise ValueError(s)

450	    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["addr","name","access","exists_cond",
451	        "implemented","transported","gate_or_disposition","reset_value",

459	for a, n in over: print("  0x%03X %s" % (a, n))
460	if not over: print("  none (matches the clean cold-cache PB csr sweep)")
461	print("\nUNDER-CLAIMS (RTL-existent + transportable disposition, not claimed, no EXCL_*):")
462	for t in under: print("  %s %s dec=%s gate=%s impl=%s" % t)
463	if not under: print("  none")
464	# sanity: baseline sample values

466	          "mhsp_ctl","msp_bound","msp_base","uitb","mcountinhibit","tselect",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ax46mpv_advanced engine registration: CSR manifest + both-direction completeness check.

Sources (the three-way audit):
  SPEC : AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7 Table 13 + per-CSR IM Requirement (curated below)
  CONFIG: build config.inc (parsed) + resolved RTL localparams (traced from the
          BUILD copy of ax46mpv_core_top.v / kv_ipipe.v -- provenance in comments)
  RTL  : existent_csr equation from the BUILD kv_csr_dec.v, machine-evaluated

Empirical:
  - transported (claimed) set: sim_ax46mpv_advanced --describe andes_csrs
    (crosschecked against scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py -- parity OK)
  - reset values: the reset-baseline capture ~/.cache/andesim/*.bin
    (hybrid_state_v1, drained from the freshly reset halted hart; fields the
    drain does not read stay zero and are reported as "-")
  - over-claim proof: the cold-cache hybrid --verify run (PB csr sweep of the
    full claimed set faulted on nothing; [state-diff] PASS 145 fields)
"""
import csv, re, struct, sys, glob, os

AND = "/home/nick/work/andesim"
VS  = "/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim"
DEC = VS + "/build/Vax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v"
OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."

# F3: when ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV points at a `sim_<engine> --probe` CSV
# (addr,yes|no,0xreset), MEASURE implemented + reset from it instead of the
# hand-traced RTL params P (below) and the ELF-keyed baseline capture. The two
# agree on this engine (validated: 0 existence mismatches, all reset values
# identical); the probe removes the manual P transcription.
_probe = {}
if os.getenv("ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV"):
    for _ln in open(os.getenv("ANDESIM_PROBE_CSV")):
        _c = _ln.strip().split(",")
        if len(_c) == 3 and _c[0].startswith("0x"):
            _probe[int(_c[0], 16)] = (_c[1] == "yes",
                                      None if _c[2] == "-" else int(_c[2], 16))

# ---- resolved RTL parameters for THIS build (traced from build sources) ----
# literals: ax46mpv_core_top.v localparams; derived ones resolved with the
# config.inc values shown in the trace (ICACHE 64K, DCACHE 64K, all ECC none,
# UTAG=1, IMPD=1, ISA_ANDES=1, BRANCH_PREDICTION=4, ACE=1).
P = dict(
    FLEN=64,                    # ax45mpv_complex.v localparam
    RVN_SUPPORT_INT=0, RVV_SUPPORT_INT=1, DSP_SUPPORT_INT=0,
    ACE_SUPPORT_INT=1, BFLOAT16_ARITH_SUPPORT=1,
    NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1, SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT=0, PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT=1,
    POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT=0, STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT=0,
    CACHE_SUPPORT_INT=1,        # ICACHE 64K / DCACHE 64K
    ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT=0, ECC_SUPPORT_INT=0,
    MMISC_CTL_EXIST_INT=1, MMSC_CFG2_EXIST_INT=0, MMSC_CFG3_EXIST_INT=1,
    MRVARCH_CFG_EXIST_INT=1, MRVARCH_CFG2_EXIST_INT=0,
    ILM_SIZE_KB=64, DLM_SIZE_KB=32, PMA_ENTRIES=4, PPI_SIZE_KB=0,
    L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0,
)
def verilog_to_py(expr: str) -> str:
    expr = re.sub(r"12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)", lambda m: "0x" + m.group(1), expr)
    return expr.replace("1'b0", "0").replace("1'b1", "1")

src = open(DEC).read()
LP = {n: int(v, 16) for n, v in
      re.findall(r"localparam\s+(CSR12_\w+)\s*=\s*12'h([0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*;", src)}
assert LP, "no CSR12_* localparams found -- decoder format changed?"
m = re.search(r"assign existent_csr = (.*?);", src, re.S)
EXISTENT = verilog_to_py(m.group(1))
# only the wires the equation actually uses (others reference runtime signals)
WIRES = {}
for n in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bs\d+\b", EXISTENT))):
    m = re.search(r"wire\s+%s\s*=\s*(.*?);" % n, src, re.S)
    assert m, "wire %s not found" % n
    WIRES[n] = verilog_to_py(m.group(1))

def implemented(addr: int) -> bool:
    if _probe and addr in _probe:
        return _probe[addr][0]
    # not in the probe: either no probe at all, or a read-side-effect CSR
    # excluded from the probe list (reading it perturbs state) -- fall back to
    # the RTL existence equation, which is exactly the cross-check the probe
    # cannot replace for these few CSRs.
    ns = dict(P); ns.update(LP); ns["csr_addr"] = addr
    for n, e in WIRES.items():
        ns[n] = int(bool(eval(e, {}, ns)))
    return bool(eval(EXISTENT, {}, ns))

# ---- the engine's claimed (transported) set ----
# gated names exactly as sim_ax46mpv_advanced --describe reported (parity with
# scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py on the build config.inc verified).
import subprocess, json as _json
DESCRIBE = _json.loads(subprocess.run(
    [VS + "/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium", "--describe"],
    capture_output=True, text=True).stdout).get("andes_csrs", [])
assert DESCRIBE, "empty --describe andes_csrs"
NAME2ADDR = {  # HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST + HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST (state_abi.h)
    "mxstatus":0x7C4,"mpft_ctl":0x7C5,"mclk_ctl":0x7DF,"milmb":0x7C0,
    "mdlmb":0x7C1,"mecc_code":0x7C2,"mhsp_ctl":0x7C6,"msp_bound":0x7C7,
    "msp_base":0x7C8,"mcountermask_m":0x7D1,"uitb":0x800,"jvt":0x017,
    "ucode":0x801,
    "menvcfg":0x30A,"mseccfg":0x747,"mcounteren":0x306,"mcountinhibit":0x320,
    "mhpmcounter3":0xB03,"mhpmcounter4":0xB04,"mhpmcounter5":0xB05,
    "mhpmcounter6":0xB06,"mhpmevent3":0x323,"mhpmevent4":0x324,
    "mhpmevent5":0x325,"mhpmevent6":0x326,"mcounterwen":0x7CE,
    "mcounterinten":0x7CF,"mcountermask_s":0x7D2,"mcountermask_u":0x7D3,
    "mnscratch":0x740,"mnepc":0x741,"mncause":0x742,"mnstatus":0x744,
    "mnvec":0x7C3,"mrnxvec":0x7DE,"mdcause":0x7C9,"mslideleg":0x7D5,
    "msavestatus":0x7D6,"msaveepc1":0x7D7,"msavecause1":0x7D8,
    "msaveepc2":0x7D9,"msavecause2":0x7DA,"msavedcause1":0x7DB,
    "msavedcause2":0x7DC,"mtvt":0x307,"mintthresh":0x347,"mcirq_entry":0x7EC,
    "mstateen0":0x30C,"mstateen1":0x30D,"mstateen2":0x30E,"mstateen3":0x30F,
    "mcctlbeginaddr":0x7CB,"mcctldata":0x7CD,"mppib":0x7F0,"mfiob":0x7F1,
    "tselect":0x7A0,"tdata1":0x7A1,"tdata2":0x7A2,"tcontrol":0x7A5,
    "mcontext":0x7A8,"uzobctl":0x808,"ucctlbeginaddr":0x80B,
    "sleepvalue":0x811,"umisc_ctl":0x813,
}
claimed = set()
for n in DESCRIBE:
    if n == "pmacfg":   claimed |= {0xBC0, 0xBC2}
    elif n == "pmaaddr": claimed |= set(range(0xBD0, 0xBE0))
    else:               claimed.add(NAME2ADDR[n])
# base always-transported standard block (hybrid_state_v1 core fields):
# restored at resume; mtvec/mstatus/mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl/pmp restored but not
# re-drained (passthrough); fflags/frm ride fcsr.
BASE = {0x300:"mstatus",0x341:"mepc",0x305:"mtvec",0x342:"mcause",
        0x343:"mtval",0x340:"mscratch",0x344:"mip",0x304:"mie",
        0xB00:"mcycle",0xB02:"minstret",0x003:"fcsr",0x001:"fflags",
        0x002:"frm",0x7CA:"mcache_ctl",0x7D0:"mmisc_ctl"}
claimed |= set(BASE)
claimed |= set(range(0x3A0, 0x3B0, 2))   # pmpcfg even (wire format, passthrough)
claimed |= set(range(0x3B0, 0x3F0))      # pmpaddr0-63
# drain-record only (in the wire format but NOT restored/re-read; S-mode
# deferred): medeleg 0x302, mideleg 0x303, satp 0x180 -> NOT claimed here.

# which claimed CSRs ride the drain (baseline reset value is real):
DRAINED = set(NAME2ADDR[n] for n in DESCRIBE if n not in ("pmacfg","pmaaddr"))
DRAINED |= {0xBC0,0xBC2} | set(range(0xBD0,0xBE0))
DRAINED |= {0x340,0x341,0x342,0x343,0x304,0x344,0xB00,0xB02,0x003,0x001,0x002}

# ---- reset-baseline capture (hybrid_state_v1) ----
st = os.stat(AND + "/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf")
bins = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser(
    "~/.cache/andesim/sim_ax45mpv_premium-*-%d-%d.bin" % (int(st.st_mtime), st.st_size)))
assert len(bins) == 1, ("need exactly the rt_c_hello baseline capture", bins)
blob = open(bins[0], "rb").read()
def u64(off): return struct.unpack_from("<Q", blob, off)[0]
ANDES_SCALARS = ["mxstatus","mpft_ctl","mclk_ctl","milmb","mdlmb","mecc_code",
                 "mhsp_ctl","msp_bound","msp_base","mcountermask_m","uitb",
                 "jvt","ucode"]
M_EXT = ["menvcfg","mseccfg","mcounteren","mcountinhibit","mhpmcounter3",
         "mhpmcounter4","mhpmcounter5","mhpmcounter6","mhpmevent3","mhpmevent4",
         "mhpmevent5","mhpmevent6","mcounterwen","mcounterinten",
         "mcountermask_s","mcountermask_u","mnscratch","mnepc","mncause",
         "mnstatus","mnvec","mrnxvec","mdcause","mslideleg","msavestatus",
         "msaveepc1","msavecause1","msaveepc2","msavecause2","msavedcause1",
         "msavedcause2","mtvt","mintthresh","mcirq_entry","mstateen0",
         "mstateen1","mstateen2","mstateen3","mcctlbeginaddr","mcctldata",
         "mppib","mfiob","tselect","tdata1","tdata2","tcontrol","mcontext",
         "uzobctl","ucctlbeginaddr","sleepvalue","umisc_ctl"]
OFF_BASE = 544  # mstatus
base_fields = ["mstatus","mepc","mtvec","mcause","mtval","mscratch","medeleg",
               "mideleg","mip","mie","mcycle","minstret","satp"]
val = {}
for i, f in enumerate(base_fields):
    val[f] = u64(OFF_BASE + 8*i)
for i in range(16): val["pmpcfg%d" % i] = u64(648 + 8*i)
for i in range(64): val["pmpaddr%d" % i] = u64(776 + 8*i)
val["fcsr"] = u64(5440); val["mcache_ctl"] = u64(5448); val["mmisc_ctl"] = u64(5456)
for i, f in enumerate(ANDES_SCALARS): val[f] = u64(5464 + 8*i)
val["pmacfg0"] = u64(5464 + 8*13); val["pmacfg2"] = u64(5464 + 8*14)
for i in range(16): val["pmaaddr%d" % i] = u64(5464 + 8*15 + 8*i)
for i, f in enumerate(M_EXT): val[f] = u64(5712 + 8*i)
val["fflags"] = val["fcsr"] & 0x1F
val["frm"] = (val["fcsr"] >> 5) & 0x7

ADDR2FIELD = {v: k for k, v in NAME2ADDR.items()}
for i, f in enumerate(base_fields): ADDR2FIELD[[0x300,0x341,0x305,0x342,0x343,0x340,0x302,0x303,0x344,0x304,0xB00,0xB02,0x180][i]] = f
ADDR2FIELD[0x003] = "fcsr"; ADDR2FIELD[0x001] = "fflags"; ADDR2FIELD[0x002] = "frm"
ADDR2FIELD[0x7CA] = "mcache_ctl"; ADDR2FIELD[0x7D0] = "mmisc_ctl"
ADDR2FIELD[0xBC0] = "pmacfg0"; ADDR2FIELD[0xBC2] = "pmacfg2"
for i in range(16): ADDR2FIELD[0xBD0 + i] = "pmaaddr%d" % i

def reset_of(addr):
    if addr not in DRAINED: return None
    if _probe:
        v = _probe.get(addr)
        return v[1] if v else None
    f = ADDR2FIELD.get(addr)
    return None if f is None else val[f]

# ---- caps gate per claimed/coverage row (mirror of andes_caps) ----
GATE = {0x7C4:"ALWAYS",0x7C5:"POWERBRAKE",0x7DF:"ALWAYS",0x7C0:"ILM",
        0x7C1:"DLM",0x7C2:"ECC",0x7C6:"STACKSAFE",0x7C7:"STACKSAFE",
        0x7C8:"STACKSAFE",0x7D1:"PMNDS_UMODE",0x800:"CODENSE",0x017:"ZCMT",
        0x801:"DSP",0x30A:"UMODE",0x747:"EPMP",0x306:"UMODE",
        0x320:"PERF_MONITOR",0xB03:"PERF_MONITOR",0xB04:"PERF_MONITOR",
        0xB05:"PERF_MONITOR",0xB06:"PERF_MONITOR",0x323:"PERF_MONITOR",
        0x324:"PERF_MONITOR",0x325:"PERF_MONITOR",0x326:"PERF_MONITOR",
        0x7CE:"PMNDS_UMODE",0x7CF:"PMNDS",0x7D2:"PMNDS_SMODE",
        0x7D3:"PMNDS_UMODE",0x740:"SMRNMI",0x741:"SMRNMI",0x742:"SMRNMI",
        0x744:"SMRNMI",0x7C3:"ALWAYS",0x7DE:"SMRNMI",0x7C9:"ALWAYS",
        0x7D5:"SMODE",0x7D6:"EXCSLVL",0x7D7:"EXCSLVL",0x7D8:"EXCSLVL",
        0x7D9:"EXCSLVL",0x7DA:"EXCSLVL",0x7DB:"EXCSLVL",0x7DC:"EXCSLVL",
        0x307:"CLIC",0x347:"CLIC",0x7EC:"CLIC",0x30C:"SMSTATEEN",
        0x30D:"SMSTATEEN",0x30E:"SMSTATEEN",0x30F:"SMSTATEEN",0x7CB:"CCTL",
        0x7CD:"CCTL",0x7F0:"PPI",0x7F1:"FIO",0x7A0:"TRIGGER",0x7A1:"TRIGGER",
        0x7A2:"TRIGGER",0x7A5:"TRIGGER",0x7A8:"TRIGGER",0x808:"UMODE",
        0x80B:"UMODE",0x811:"UMODE",0x813:"ALT_FP"}
GATE_ON = {"ALWAYS":1,"POWERBRAKE":0,"ILM":1,"DLM":1,"ECC":0,"STACKSAFE":0,
           "PMNDS":1,"PMNDS_UMODE":0,"PMNDS_SMODE":0,"CODENSE":1,"ZCMT":0,
           "DSP":0,"UMODE":0,"EPMP":0,"PERF_MONITOR":1,"SMRNMI":0,"SMODE":0,
           "EXCSLVL":0,"CLIC":0,"SMSTATEEN":0,"CCTL":1,"ALT_FP":1,"PPI":0,
           "FIO":0,"TRIGGER":1,"PMA":1}

# ---- spec existence conditions (Table 13 + per-CSR IM Requirement) ----
EC = {}
def ec(names, cond):
    for n in names.split(): EC[n] = cond
ec("mvendorid marchid mimpid mhartid mconfigptr misa mstatus mie mtvec "
   "mscratch mepc mcause mtval mip mcycle minstret mcountinhibit "
   "micm_cfg mdcm_cfg mmsc_cfg mxstatus mdcause dcsr dpc dscratch0 "
   "dscratch1 dexc2dbg ddcause", "Always")
ec("mhpmcounter3~6 mhpmevent3~6", "Always (OF/*INH fields: mrvarch_cfg.sscofpmf==1)")
ec("mcounterinten mcounterovf", "mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1")
ec("mcounterwen mcountermask_m mcountermask_u", "mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[20]==1")
ec("mcountermask_s", "mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1")
ec("scountermask_m scountermask_s scountermask_u scounterinten scounterovf "
   "scountinhibit shpmevent3~6", "mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1")
ec("scountovf", "mrvarch_cfg.sscofpmf==1 & misa[18]==1")
ec("mcycleh minstreth mhpmcounter3h~6h mhpmevent3h~6h", "Always (RV32 only)")
ec("mcounteren", "misa[20]==1")
ec("scounteren", "misa[18]==1")
ec("medeleg mideleg", "misa[18]==1 | misa[13]==1")
ec("menvcfg", "misa[20]==1")
ec("menvcfgh", "misa[20]==1 (RV32 only)")
ec("mslideleg slie slip", "misa[18]==1")
ec("sstatus sie sip sscratch stval stvec sepc scause sdcause sedeleg sideleg "
   "senvcfg", "misa[18]==1")
ec("mcctlbeginaddr mcctlcommand mcctldata",
   "(micm_cfg.ISZ!=0 | mdcm_cfg.DSZ!=0) & mmsc_cfg.CCTLCSR==1")
ec("ucctlbeginaddr ucctlcommand",
   "misa[20]==1 & (micm_cfg.ISZ!=0 | mdcm_cfg.DSZ!=0) & mmsc_cfg.CCTLCSR==1")
ec("scctldata", "misa[18]==1 & (micm_cfg.ISZ!=0 | mdcm_cfg.DSZ!=0) & mmsc_cfg.CCTLCSR==1")
ec("pmpcfg0 pmpcfg2 pmpcfg4~15 pmpaddr0 pmpaddr1~63",
   "Always (WARL probe detects entry count)")
ec("pmpcfg1 pmpcfg3", "Always (RV32 only)")
ec("tselect mcontrol/tdata1 tdata2 tcontrol mcontext tinfo", "Trigger Module optional")
ec("tdata3", "Trigger Module optional (always returns 0)")
ec("scontext", "Trigger Module optional & misa[18]==1")
ec("mrnxvec mnscratch mnepc mncause mnstatus", "mrvarch_cfg3.Smrnmi==1")
ec("mnvec", "Required (per-CSR section 9.x; base Andes NMI vector)")
ec("mmsc_cfg2", "misa.MXL==1 & mmsc_cfg.msc_ext==1 (RV32 only)")
ec("mmsc_cfg3", "mmsc_cfg.msc_ext3==1 (RV64)")
ec("mmsc_cfg4", "mmsc_cfg3.msc_ext4==1 (RV32)")
ec("mvec_cfg", "misa.V==1 & mmsc_cfg.veccfg==1")
ec("mrvarch_cfg", "mmsc_cfg.RVARCH==1 (RV64)")
ec("mrvarch_cfg2", "misa.MXL==1 & mmsc_cfg2.RVARCH2==1 (RV32 only)")
ec("mrvarch_cfg3", "mrvarch_cfg.MRVARCH_EXT3==1 (RV64)")
ec("mccache_ctl_base", "mmsc_cfg.CCACHE==1")
ec("milmb", "micm_cfg.ILMB!=0")
ec("mdlmb", "mdcm_cfg.DLMB!=0")
ec("mecc_code", "mmsc_cfg.ECC==1")
ec("mhsp_ctl msp_bound msp_base", "mmsc_cfg.HSP==1 | mmsc_cfg.HSPO==1")
ec("mpft_ctl", "mmsc_cfg.PFT==1")
ec("mcache_ctl", "micm_cfg.ISZ!=0 | mdcm_cfg.DSZ!=0")

ec("mmisc_ctl", "mmsc_cfg.AEC==1 | mmsc_cfg.VPLIC==1 | mmsc_cfg.ECD==1 | mmsc_cfg.EV5==1")
ec("smisc_ctl", "misa[18]==1 & mmsc_cfg.AEC==1")
ec("msavestatus", "mmsc_cfg.EXCSLVL>0")
ec("msaveepc1 msavecause1 msavedcause1", "mmsc_cfg.EXCSLVL>0 | mmsc_cfg.CRASHSAVE==1")
ec("msaveepc2 msavecause2 msavedcause2", "mmsc_cfg.EXCSLVL>1")
ec("mcrash_statesave mstatus_crashsave", "mmsc_cfg.CRASHSAVE==1")
ec("mclk_ctl", "misa.V==1 | mmsc_cfg.BF16CVT==1")
ec("uitb", "mmsc_cfg.ECD==1")
ec("cycle time instret hpmcounter3~6", "misa[20]==1")
ec("cycleh timeh instreth hpmcounter3h~6h", "misa[20]==1 (RV32 only)")
ec("fflags frm fcsr", "misa[5]==1 | misa[3]==1")
ec("JVT", "Zcmt (ZCE) extension implemented")
ec("ustatus uie utvec uscratch uepc ucause utval uip udcause", "misa[13]==1")
ec("ucode", "mmsc_cfg.EDSP==1")
ec("uzobctl", "misa.V==1 | mmsc_cfg3.AMM==1 (RV64)")
ec("wfe sleepvalue txevt", "mmsc_cfg.ESLEEP==1")
ec("umisc_ctl", "mmsc_cfg.ALT_FP_FMT==1 | mmsc_cfg3.CST_CTL==1 (RV64)")
ec("mtvt mnxti mintstatus mintthresh mscratchcsw mscratchcswl",
   "mmsc_cfg.CLIC==1")
ec("stvt snxti sintstatus sintthresh sscratchcsw sscratchcswl",
   "mmsc_cfg.CLIC==1 & misa[18]==1")
ec("mirq_entry mintsel_jal pushmcause pushmepc pushmxstatus", "mmsc_cfg.ECLIC==1")
ec("mppib", "mmsc_cfg.PPI==1")
ec("mfiob", "mmsc_cfg.FIO==1")
ec("pmacfg0 pmacfg2 pmaaddr0~15", "mmsc_cfg.PPMA==1")
ec("pmacfg4 pmacfg6 pmacfg8 pmacfg10",
   "mmsc_cfg.PPMA==1 & (mmsc_cfg3.PPMA_VER==2 | mmsc_cfg4.PPMA_VER==2)")
ec("pmacfg1 pmacfg3", "mmsc_cfg.PPMA==1 (RV32 only)")
ec("pmacfg5 pmacfg7 pmacfg9 pmacfg11",
   "mmsc_cfg.PPMA==1 & mmsc_cfg4.PPMA_VER==2 (RV32 only)")
ec("pmaaddr0~47", "mmsc_cfg.PPMA==1 (0-15); 16-47 also need PPMA_VER==2")
ec("satp", "misa[18]==1")
ec("mseccfg", "Optional (Smepmp / Zkr)")
ec("mseccfgh", "Optional (Smepmp / Zkr) (RV32 only)")
ec("mstateen0 mstateen1 mstateen2 mstateen3", "Smstateen implemented")
ec("mstateen0h mstateen1h mstateen2h mstateen3h", "Smstateen implemented (RV32 only)")
ec("sstateen0 sstateen1 sstateen2 sstateen3", "Smstateen implemented & misa[18]==1")
ec("miselect mireg mireg2 mireg3 mireg4 mireg5 mireg6",
   "Smcsrind (indirect CSR access) implemented")
ec("siselect sireg sireg2 sireg3 sireg4 sireg5 sireg6",
   "Sscsrind implemented & misa[18]==1")
ec("vsiselect vsireg vsireg2 vsireg3 vsireg4 vsireg5 vsireg6",
   "Sscsrind implemented & misa[7]==1 (H)")
ec("hstatus hedeleg hideleg hie hcounteren hgeie", "misa[7]==1 (H)")
ec("mpl2cm_cfg", "mmsc_cfg3.PL2C==1")
ec("ml1dbf_cfg", "mmsc_cfg3.L1D_BF==1 (RV64)")
ec("mhvm_cfg mhvmb", "mmsc_cfg3.HVMCSR==1")

def cond_for(name):
    n = name.replace("ﬁ", "fi").replace("ﬂ", "fl")  # PDF ligatures
    return EC.get(n, EC.get(n.replace("~", "~"), "-"))

# ---- inventory rows ----
def expand(addr_field):
    """inventory addr string -> list of ints"""
    s = addr_field.strip()
    m = re.match(r"^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$", s)
    if m: return [int(m.group(1), 16)]
    m = re.match(r"^0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)~(?:0x)?([0-9A-Fa-f]+)$", s)
    if m:
        lo = int(m.group(1), 16); hi_s = m.group(2)
        hi = int(m.group(1)[: len(m.group(1)) - len(hi_s)] + hi_s, 16) \
             if len(hi_s) < len(m.group(1)) else int(hi_s, 16)
        return list(range(lo, hi + 1))
    raise ValueError(s)

def compact(addrs):
    """compact sorted addr list -> '0xBD0-0xBDF' / 'even 0x3A4-0x3AE' / list"""
    a = sorted(addrs)
    if len(a) > 2 and all(y - x == 1 for x, y in zip(a, a[1:])):
        return "0x%X-0x%X" % (a[0], a[-1])
    if len(a) > 2 and all(y - x == 2 for x, y in zip(a, a[1:])):
        return "even 0x%X-0x%X" % (a[0], a[-1])
    return ",".join("0x%X" % x for x in a)

TRANSPORTABLE = {"TRANSPORT_NOW", "NEW", "NEW_TRIG", "NEW_UDELTA"}
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(AND + "/tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv")))
out_rows, under, over, impl_count = [], [], [], 0
for r in rows:
    addrs = expand(r["addr"])
    name = r["name"].replace("ﬁ", "fi").replace("ﬂ", "fl")
    impl = [a for a in addrs if implemented(a)]
    claim = [a for a in addrs if a in claimed]
    impl_v = "yes" if len(impl) == len(addrs) else ("partial" if impl else "no")
    tr_v   = "yes" if len(claim) == len(addrs) else ("partial" if claim else "no")
    if impl: impl_count += len(impl)
    dec = r["decision"]
    # gate/disposition text
    if claim:
        if addrs[0] in GATE:
            g = GATE[addrs[0]]
        elif 0x3A0 <= addrs[0] <= 0x3EF:
            g = "BASE_PMP(passthrough; restored for S/U handoffs only)"
        elif addrs[0] in (0xBC0, 0xBC2) or 0xBD0 <= addrs[0] <= 0xBDF or r["name"].startswith("pma"):
            g = "PMA"
        elif addrs[0] in (0x7CA, 0x7D0):
            g = "BASE(restored, not re-drained)"
        elif addrs[0] in (0x300, 0x305):
            g = "BASE(restored; " + ("verify via passthrough)" if addrs[0]==0x300 else "not re-drained)")
        elif addrs[0] in (0x001, 0x002):
            g = "BASE_FP(via fcsr)"
        elif addrs[0] == 0x003:
            g = "BASE_FP"
        elif addrs[0] == 0x344:
            g = "BASE(restored+re-read; verify-excluded: HW-driven bits)"
        elif addrs[0] in (0xB00, 0xB02):
            g = "BASE(counter; verify-excluded)"
        else:
            g = "BASE"
        if tr_v == "partial":
            g += "; claimed=" + compact(claim)
    else:
        if dec in TRANSPORTABLE:
            if addrs[0] in GATE:
                g = "%s[gate %s=off]" % (dec, GATE[addrs[0]])
            elif not impl:
                g = dec + "[not implemented on this engine]"
            elif addrs[0] in (0x302, 0x303, 0x180):
                g = dec + "[drain-record only; S-mode, not restored]"
            else:
                g = dec
        else:
            g = dec
    # reset value
    rv = [reset_of(a) for a in addrs]
    rv = [v for v in rv if v is not None]
    if not rv: rv_s = "-"
    elif len(set(rv)) == 1: rv_s = "0x%X" % rv[0]
    else: rv_s = " ".join("0x%X" % v for v in rv)
    # verify treatment (driver state_diff.cpp kExcluded + passthrough rules)
    VEXCL = {"msp_bound":"reset-divergent","msp_base":"reset-divergent",
             "milmb":"EN-bit HW-presence","mdlmb":"EN-bit HW-presence",
             "mhpmcounter3":"ticks in ROI","mhpmcounter4":"ticks in ROI",
             "mhpmcounter5":"ticks in ROI","mhpmcounter6":"ticks in ROI",
             "mdcause":"HW-set","tdata1":"WARL+reset divergence","tcontrol":"WARL+reset divergence",
             "mcontext":"WARL+reset divergence","mnvec":"reset-divergent (QEMU 0 vs reset vector)",
             "mip":"HW-driven bits","mcycle":"counter","minstret":"counter",
             "mstatus":"passthrough","mtvec":"passthrough",
             "mcache_ctl":"restored, not re-drained","mmisc_ctl":"restored, not re-drained"}
    if tr_v == "no":
        vf = "-"
    elif name in VEXCL:
        vf = "excluded:" + VEXCL[name]
    elif name.startswith("pmp"):
        vf = "excluded:passthrough (M-mode runs)"
    else:
        vf = "compared"
    # safe-write policy: the reviewed table tests/engines/safe_write_policy.csv
    # is the authority; rows it does not name await review.
    import csv as _csv, os as _os
    _pol = getattr(sys.modules[__name__], "_POLICY", None)
    if _pol is None:
        _pp = _os.path.join(_os.path.dirname(_os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "safe_write_policy.csv")
        _pol = {q["name"]: q["action"] for q in _csv.DictReader(open(_pp))}
        setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "_POLICY", _pol)
    def _polname(nm):
        m2 = re.match(r"^(.*?)(\d+)~(\d+)$", nm)
        return (m2.group(1) + m2.group(2)) if m2 else nm
    act = _pol.get(_polname(name))
    if tr_v == "no" or r["priv"].endswith("RO"):
        sw = "-"
    elif act == "write":
        sw = "fixture(policy)"
    elif act == "readback":
        sw = "readback(policy)"
    elif act == "covered":
        sw = "covered(engine-generic fixture)"
    elif act == "verify-only":
        sw = "verify-only(policy)"
    else:
        sw = "review-pending"
    out_rows.append(dict(addr=r["addr"], name=name, access=r["priv"],
                         exists_cond=cond_for(name), implemented=impl_v,
                         transported=tr_v, gate_or_disposition=g,
                         reset_value=rv_s, verify=vf, safe_write=sw))
    # completeness both directions
    for a in addrs:
        if a in claimed and a not in impl:
            over.append((a, name))
    if impl and dec in TRANSPORTABLE and not claim:
        under.append((r["addr"], name, dec,
                      GATE.get(addrs[0], "?"),
                      ["0x%X" % a for a in impl]))

os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(OUT, "csr_manifest.csv"), "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["addr","name","access","exists_cond",
        "implemented","transported","gate_or_disposition","reset_value",
        "verify","safe_write"])
    w.writeheader(); w.writerows(out_rows)

print("rows:", len(out_rows))
print("engine-implemented inventory CSR addresses:", impl_count)
print("claimed set size:", len(claimed))
print("\nOVER-CLAIMS (claimed but not RTL-existent; PMP excluded as passthrough):")
for a, n in over: print("  0x%03X %s" % (a, n))
if not over: print("  none (matches the clean cold-cache PB csr sweep)")
print("\nUNDER-CLAIMS (RTL-existent + transportable disposition, not claimed, no EXCL_*):")
for t in under: print("  %s %s dec=%s gate=%s impl=%s" % t)
if not under: print("  none")
# sanity: baseline sample values
for k in ("mepc","mcause","mie","mcycle","minstret","mxstatus","milmb","mdlmb",
          "mhsp_ctl","msp_bound","msp_base","uitb","mcountinhibit","tselect",
          "tdata1","tcontrol","mdcause","pmacfg0","fcsr","mscratch","mtval",
          "mip","mhpmcounter3","mhpmevent3","mcontext","tdata2","pmaaddr0",
          "mpft_ctl","mclk_ctl","mcache_ctl","mmisc_ctl","mstatus","mtvec"):
    print("  reset[%s] = 0x%X" % (k, val[k]))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch a Jupyter Lab server reachable from a remote browser.
#
# Usage:  scripts/notebook_server.sh [port]     (default: 8888)
#
# Needs only `uv` on the host: uvx downloads and caches JupyterLab on the
# first run, so there is no permanent install. The server binds 0.0.0.0 with
# auth disabled: anyone who can reach the port gets full access.
set -euo pipefail

PORT="${1:-${PORT:-8888}}"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

# This machine's LAN IP, for the URL a remote browser should use.
IP="$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<NF;i++) if($i=="src") print $(i+1)}')"
IP="${IP:-$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')}"

echo "Open from a remote browser:"
echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab"
echo "CSR coverage sheet directly:"
echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab/tree/docs/csr_coverage.ipynb"
echo

exec uvx --from jupyterlab jupyter-lab \
    --ip 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --no-browser \
    --IdentityProvider.token="" \
    --ServerApp.password="" \
    --notebook-dir "$REPO_ROOT"

content.text:
no findings would be inaccurate — here are the altitude findings.

---

**Finding A — the whole per-engine `gen_manifest.py` is a fork that diverges only in one data block**
- `file`: `tests/engines/ax45mpv_premium-5bea8bdc/gen_manifest.py` (and its twin `tests/engines/ax46mpv_advanced-a13f86a3/gen_manifest.py`)
- `line`: 43 (the `P = dict(...)` block — the *only* genuinely per-engine content)
- `summary`: Two ~470-line generators are byte-identical from line ~211 to the end (the `GATE`/`EC`/`NAME2ADDR` spec tables, the `hybrid_state_v1` byte-offset layout, the entire row-emit loop, `VEXCL`, the policy join, the writer). They differ only in the `P` RTL-parameter dict, the hardcoded engine name (`DEC` line 23, `--describe` subprocess line 89-91, cache glob line 138-140), and a hand-adapted `implemented()` wire-extraction (lines 66-71 vs the twin's named-helper form).
- `cost`: Every new engine/config re-forks 400+ shared lines. The two copies have *already* drifted in logic, not just data — `implemented()` evaluates all `s\d+` wires generically here but only three named wires in the twin — so a fix or spec-table correction to one silently fails to reach the other. Evidence of blind copy: line 1's docstring says "ax46mpv_advanced engine registration" inside the ax45 file, and `GATE_ON` (line 206) is a hand-maintained per-engine caps table that nothing consumes (dead duplicated data that must still be kept in sync by hand).
- `deeper fix`: One shared `tests/engines/gen_manifest.py` parameterized by the registration dir: derive the engine name from `regdir.name.rsplit("-",1)[0]` (as `gen_fixtures.py` already does), load the per-engine `P`/params from a small data file inside the regdir, and keep the spec tables + struct layout + emit loop in the single script. Per-engine dirs then carry data, not code.

**Finding B — the config-identity hash recipe is copy-pasted into three places with no shared helper**
- `file`: `tests/engines/test_registration_guard.sh`
- `line`: 28 (`hash=$(grep -v '^// created on ' "$CFG" | sha256sum | cut -c1-8)`)
- `summary`: The exact normalize-then-hash recipe that defines an engine's registration identity is hardcoded in the guard (line 28) and re-typed as prose in both `engine.env` recompute comments (`ax45mpv_premium-5bea8bdc/engine.env:3`, `ax46mpv_advanced-a13f86a3/engine.env:3`).
- `cost`: The just-added `grep -v '^// created on '` filter had to be applied in all three spots at once; the next change to the timestamp/preamble format (e.g. a second generated line) will silently make the per-engine `engine.env` instructions produce a different hash than the gate, and every future `engine.env` re-hardcodes the drifting recipe.
- `deeper fix`: A single `scripts/config_hash.sh <config.inc>` (or shared shell function) that emits the 8-hex identity; the guard calls it and the `engine.env` comment just points at it, so the normalization rule lives in exactly one place.

**Finding C — the CSR address/name range grammar is re-parsed by four independent reimplementations**
- `file`: `tests/engines/probe_engine.sh`
- `line`: 41 (inline Python `def expand(s)` with the truncated-suffix `0xADDR~ADDR` logic)
- `summary`: `probe_engine.sh`'s inline `expand` is a near-verbatim copy of `gen_manifest.py`'s addr-range `expand` (line ~317); separately the name-range collapse `^(.*?)(\d+)~(\d+)$` is re-implemented in `gen_fixtures.py:44`, `check_test_coverage.py:41`, and `gen_manifest.py`'s `_polname`.
- `cost`: The `0xADDR~ADDR` / `nameLO~HI` grammar is now spelled out in four spots that already differ (some handle a `~0x` prefix, some the truncated-suffix form); extending the inventory notation means finding and matching all four, and a probe that parses a range differently than the manifest generator produces mismatched existence data.
- `deeper fix`: One shared range-expansion utility (a tiny `csr_ranges.py` importable by the Python tools, invoked by the probe) that both `expand(addr)` and `collapse(name)->key` live in — a single grammar definition.

**Finding D — the coverage check re-derives a verdict the generator already materialized, and re-encodes the action vocabulary**
- `file`: `tests/engines/check_test_coverage.py`
- `line`: 35 (`ALLOWED = {"write","readback","covered","verify-only"}`)
- `summary`: `gen_manifest.py` already joins `safe_write_policy.csv` and writes the per-CSR verdict into the manifest's `safe_write` column (`readback(policy)` / `verify-only(policy)` / `review-pending` / ...). The check re-loads `safe_write_policy.csv`, re-runs the `polname` range-collapse (third copy, see Finding C), and hardcodes the valid-action set again — the same vocabulary the generator's else-chain encodes (lines 424-434 of `gen_manifest.py`).
- `cost`: The set of legal policy actions now lives in three files (generator's mapping, `gen_fixtures.py`'s write/readback branch, and this `ALLOWED`); adding an action means editing all three, and the check can disagree with the manifest it is supposed to be guarding.
- `deeper fix`: Have the transported→tested gate read the manifest's own generated `safe_write` column (the single materialized source of truth) and fail on `review-pending`/`-`, rather than independently re-joining the policy CSV and re-listing the vocabulary.
